title: Navigating a Career in Entomology with a Chronic Illness
content: The pandemic of 2020 impacted most of us: isolation, challenges with mental health, delays in research, and much more. These impacts were especially felt by students in critical parts of their degrees. I, for one, had arrived at my candidacy in the second year of my Ph.D. at Kansas State University during the height of the pandemic in the spring of 2020. I was able to meet that challenge and pass; however, my physical health began to decline suddenly. By the beginning of 2021, I found myself dealing with undiagnosed vascular symptoms and excruciating pain in my legs. I had no appetite and I was losing weight. I knew that something had to be wrong, so I sought medical assistance. After 6 months of working with doctors, I received a diagnosis—primary Sjögren’s Syndrome, a systemic autoimmune disease, and autoimmune leukocytoclastic vasculitis. I never imagined myself being diagnosed with a chronic illness, and I did not even know what an autoimmune disease was. I remember hearing when I was younger that Selena Gomez, a popular actress and singer, had been diagnosed with lupus. Now I was facing a similar challenge. My life changed forever, but I was relieved that I had been diagnosed sooner than most.
